result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.mutate_node_attrs_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Transform a node attribute using a function on selected nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7903-L7988){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.mutate_node_attrs_ws( node_attr, func, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies a transformation function to the specified attribute for all selected nodes. The function receives each node's current attribute value and returns the new value. Requires an active node selection. Nodes without the specified attribute are skipped. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the attribute to transform. [func]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Transformation function that takes the current attribute value and returns the new value. Called once per selected node. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The function receives each selected node's current value and returns the replacement -- here, doubling `score` for two of the three nodes: ::: {#d5e7f344 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node('A', score=10) graph.add_node('B', score=20) graph.add_node('C', score=30) id_a = graph.get_id_from_label('A') id_b = graph.get_id_from_label('B') id_c = graph.get_id_from_label('C') (graph .select_nodes_by_id([id_a, id_b]) .mutate_node_attrs_ws('score', lambda x: x * 2) ) graph.get_node(id_a).attributes['score'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 20 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#44dc929b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node(id_b).attributes['score'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 40 ``` ::: ::: "C" was never selected, so its score is untouched: ::: {#5decb078 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node(id_c).attributes['score'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 30 ``` ::: ::: Combining this with `select_nodes()` applies the transformation only to nodes matching a condition -- here, discounting prices above `100`: ::: {#d4612395 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", price=80) .add_node(label="B", price=120) .add_node(label="C", price=150) ) ( graph .select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes.get('price', 0) > 100) .mutate_node_attrs_ws('price', lambda p: p * 0.9) ) graph.get_node_attrs("price") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {2: 108.0, 3: 135.0, 1: 80} ``` ::: :::
